business: Quilt: a phone app where an AI assistant builds and fills small life apps (budget, groceries, classes, to-dos, subscriptions) from a photo or a sentence
by_segment: Mostly supported by family or aid
why_not: I already have my Notion and a spreadsheet set up exactly how I like them, and I don't earn anything, so another $6 a month isn't happening. I might try the free version, but 5 apps and 10 photos is more than I'd actually use.

My Notes app already does my grocery list and money notes, and it's free and I never have to check anything. I might try the free version once out of curiosity, but I'm not paying $6 a month when I make like $2,000 a year.

I'm literally trying to cancel subscriptions after getting burned by a renewal this semester, so I'm not adding a $6 one. I'd maybe try the free version to catch due dates, but I'm not paying for Plus.
I don't pay for apps, period. And it's not even on iPhone yet, so I can't use the free version either. Our house Venmo request and the Notes app already handle groceries fine.
I'm on an iPhone and it says iPhone later, so I'd be stuck using a website in Safari, and my Notes app already does lists and money stuff fine. Not paying for something I can't even install.

I've got an iPhone, so it's out for now. I'm not saving a website to snap receipts from Smith's. Even if it was on iPhone I'd use the free version for a week and forget about it, and I'm not paying $6 a month for that.

It's brand new, so there are no Play ratings or Reddit threads for me to check, and I'm not paying for anything I can't read reviews on first. At most I'd poke at the free tier with a syllabus PDF, and on $4,000 a year the free version would have to fail me before I'd even think about $6.
flip: A real iPhone app where the free tier handles my groceries and budget well enough that I'd actually ditch Notes.
If it could pull in my existing Notion or spreadsheet so I didn't have to start over, and I actually kept using the free version for a full month.
If the free tier actually caught a renewal or a late fee for me and saved more than it costs, I'd think about Plus around finals.
An iPhone app with a free student plan that covers what I'd actually use, like unlimited Plus with a uNID.
A free student deal through the U, like a year of Plus free with my uNID email.
A free student plan through the U, or the Plus tier bundled with something I already pay for, like a student discount at $1 or $2 a month.
Seeing it read a crumpled corner-store receipt perfectly on the first try, and the free tier being enough that I never hit a paywall.
Solid Play Store ratings and Reddit threads from other U of U students saying the free tier actually saves them money, plus a one-time price or a cheap student price around $1-2 a month.
If the syllabus photo really dropped every due date for the semester into my calendar, I might use the free tier for that. I still wouldn't pay unless it replaced the budgeting app I already have.
A bunch of real reviews from other U of U students saying it read their receipts and syllabi correctly without much fixing, plus a student price around $2 to $3 a month.
If I actually kept using the free version for a month and it nailed my receipts and syllabus without me fixing stuff, I'd maybe pay, but only around $3 a month.
An iPhone app that's still worth opening after the first week, like if it actually stopped me running out of money before payday.
An iPhone app, and then a free month that actually kept me opening it past week one.
If it nudged me at the right moment, like after I shop, and the free tier was enough that I kept using it for a month without thinking about it.
If it actually caught every due date from my syllabi and receipts for a whole semester on the free tier and I stopped missing things, I'd think about a one-time payment, not a subscription.

If a friend showed me it reading a messy receipt perfectly and it actually caught something I'd missed with my money, I might keep using the free tier, but paying would still need a student price around $2.
If the free tier actually caught a renewal or due date before it hit me and saved me a late fee, I'd think about paying, but only at like $2 or $3 a month with a student price.

If it could pull my Notion or spreadsheet data in and keep everything I already have, and the free tier ran out halfway through a semester of syllabi and grocery runs, I'd think about Plus around $3 a month.
An iPhone app that pings me a few days before a renewal or bill is due, even if I had to add the subscriptions myself once.
A free student plan through the U, like how I get other stuff free with my uNID.
